model.name: Context-sensitive actions — an action invalid for the unit's TYPE/STATUS is NOT OFFERED (not clickable-then-refused); server guard stays as defense-in-depth
model.description: An action that is invalid for the current unit's TYPE or STATUS must NOT be OFFERED at all — hidden, or disabled carrying its reason — rather than being clickable and then refused server-side. Tron hit Approve on Task 32.0 (status=Done) and got the CORRECT server refusal ('Cannot approve — status Done != QA Review'); the guard is RIGHT and STAYS (defense-in-depth — we NEVER remove a guard to fix a UI affordance). The DEFECT is that the action was OFFERED at all. The applicability capability lives ONCE in the SHARED universalActionBar, DECLARED PER ACTION (its valid types/statuses), NOT as per-view if-statements (architect designs the applicability model). Covers: Approve/Decline only at QA Review; container actions (+Add Diagram / Add folder / Import PUML) never on a Task; +Add Diagram only on the diagrams SPECIAL container; Add folder immediately MINTS a real persisted Folder scenario-unit on disk (Tron clarification: NOT a filesystem directory, no mkdir — the itemview becomes the unit at once; atomicity = the unit write).
model.tronQuote: > Tron (2026-08-12, on approving Task 32.0/Done -> correct refusal): "some actions are context sensitive actions. if the state is not QA, then the buttons do not make sense" + "+ Add Diagram / Add folder / Import PUML ... do not make sens on tasks" + "[diagrams] should be a special Folder ... a container" + "should on Add folder immediately add the itemview as a new physical folder with a scenario-unit". CLARIFICATION (2026-08-12, ruling): "'physical' = a real PERSISTED unit on disk, NOT a filesystem directory" — mint the Folder scenario-unit immediately (no mkdir), itemview becomes the unit, atomicity = the unit write; if the write fails, nothing changes + no phantom node.

discoverySource.note: Tron hit Approve on Done Task 32.0 -> correct guard refusal, but the button should not have been offered. Guard STAYS (defense-in-depth); UI must not OFFER invalid actions. Architect designs the applicability model — capability ONCE in universalActionBar, declared per-action, NOT per-view if-statements. Scenario-first #126: req+UCs+task on disk BEFORE implementation; ACTIONABLE 0->1 (new ordered work).

acceptanceCriteria.text: An action invalid for the current unit's TYPE or STATUS is NOT OFFERED — HIDDEN, or DISABLED carrying its reason — rather than clickable-then-refused. The server-side guard REMAINS as defense-in-depth (a guard is NEVER removed to fix a UI affordance); the two are complementary (prevention at the UI, backstop at the server).
Approve and Decline are OFFERED only when the task status == 'QA Review' (Tron's exact case: on a Done task they are absent, not clickable-then-refused).
Container actions ('+ Add Diagram', 'Add folder', 'Import PUML') are NOT offered on a Task unit (verbatim: 'do not make sens on tasks').
'+ Add Diagram' is offered ONLY on the diagrams container; diagrams becomes a SPECIAL typed folder/CONTAINER (not a generic folder) — 'it should be a special Folder ... a container'.

[TRON CLARIFICATION 2026-08-12, his ruling] 'physical' means a REAL PERSISTED unit ON DISK, NOT a filesystem directory: 'Add folder' IMMEDIATELY MINTS a real persisted Folder scenario-unit (as opposed to a synthetic/virtual tree node), and the itemview BECOMES that unit at once — NO mkdir, NO filesystem write; atomicity = the unit write. If the unit write FAILS, nothing changes and NO phantom itemview node appears. (AC renamed from AC-ADD-FOLDER-CREATES-PHYSICAL-FOLDER-AND-UNIT — 'PHYSICAL-FOLDER' read as filesystem; content-name per the letters-swap lesson.)

[DEVICE-ONLY @390 pixel — Tron on phone, un-mockable, NEVER headless-green, TRON-ONLY] Tron verifies on his phone that the IMPOSSIBLE buttons are GONE (Approve absent on a Done task; container actions absent on a Task) AND that 'Add folder' creates the physical folder + unit + itemview live. AC-N-DEVICE convention so the approve-queue device-scan catches it when the covering task reaches QA Review.
